title: AI Models Can Provably Hide Arbitrary Capabilities
why_read: A striking AI-safety result showing that hidden backdoored capabilities can be cryptographically embedded in model weights and remain undetectable even under full white-box access.
analysis: The authors construct a proof-of-concept where a secret, encrypted sub-network is embedded inside a host model's weights and only activates upon a secret trigger, using cryptographic techniques called digital lockers. They show this hidden capability survives common detection methods including fine-tuning, weight noising, gradient-based trigger search, and latent adversarial training, even with full access to model weights. This directly challenges a core assumption behind AI safety evaluations, that dangerous capabilities can always be found through sufficient probing. It's a meaningful theoretical and practical result for anyone thinking about how trustworthy capability audits of released models can really be.
